text:
alex (ceo): thanks for the great Q&A today. lots of requests for clearer positioning language and concrete roadmap signals. wanted to put a short follow-up here so teams can move.

mira (vp-product): please confirm the order of priorities so PMs can update backlog priorities — is it Hosted > Dedicated > Private for product focus, or something more nuanced?

alex (ceo): nuance: keep Hosted as the fastest path for product-led growth and experimentation. prioritize Dedicated work for top pipeline accounts that will convert to ARR. Private is strategic for compliance-heavy customers; support it but don't let it derail general roadmap velocity.

lee (cto): for engineering plans: do we have explicit SLO targets that signal when to switch engineering modes (e.g., if Dedicated deals need p50<60ms for 2K qps)? would help triage infra vs feature work.

alex (ceo): good point. we'll publish a small SLO matrix: target latencies and reliability bands for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. treat that as guidance for tradeoffs. engineering leads, use it in sprint planning.

dani (head-sales): sales follow-up: what language should reps use when customers compare us to vendors that only offer "model hosting" or only "on-prem appliances"? reps get stuck on feature lists.

jess (marketing): we should provide two snippets: a one-liner for execs and a technical bullet for SEs.

alex (ceo): proposed exec one-liner: "Redwood: production-first inference — developer-friendly API, predictable performance, and flexible deployment models." technical bullet for SEs: "single runtime across deployments, workload-aware batching & prefix caching, and policy-based smart routing for cost/latency tradeoffs."

dani (head-sales): that works. can marketing make a checklist of proof points (benchmarks, case studies) to back those claims when customers push back?

jess (marketing): yes — we'll assemble quick proofs: latency distribution graphs, a 3-customer case study (hosted->dedicated migration), and an ops checklist for Private installs.

mira (vp-product): on roadmap conflicts: PMs flagged admin UX features vs kernel perf improvements. which should win if both unblock revenue?

alex (ceo): if a specific customer or set of customers ties a purchase to kernel/runtime perf, prioritize that. otherwise, incremental admin/ops features that reduce support time are high ROI too. use the SLO matrix + revenue impact to decide.

lee (cto): engineering ask: we need visibility into the "top Dedicated deals" list so we can schedule perf work. can product share that safely with engineering leads?

alex (ceo): yes — product to publish an anonymized prioritized deals list (customer, estimated ARR, required timeline). keep sensitive legal info in the sales doc vault.

ops-bot: created ticket T-5017 in #product-ops: "Produce SLO matrix + one-liner variants + Priority Deals list (anonymized)" assigned to @mira and @jess, due in 3 business days.

mira (vp-product): noted. i'll put drafts in #product-ops and link here. please DM me any specific edge cases. thanks everyone — we'll iterate quickly on the microcopy and the SLO guidance. :thumbsup:
